figures.claim: External rotation of the tibia is resisted mainly by the posterolateral corner at 30 degrees of flexion and increasingly by the posterior cruciate as flexion increases.
Measuring external rotation at 30 and at 90 degrees therefore separates a corner injury from a combined corner and posterior cruciate injury.
